title: Embedding and vector weaknesses
summary: Vector stores add risks of their own: cross-tenant leaks from missing filters, text recovered from embeddings, and poisoned vectors. OWASP covers them as LLM08.
useIf: Your index holds embeddings of private text, or several tenants and apps share one vector store.
avoidIf: You are choosing an ACL pattern. Use the access control topics and treat this as the threat background.

explain.md: OWASP LLM08:2025 names four weaknesses: unauthorized access and data leakage, cross-context leaks in multi-tenant shared vector stores, embedding inversion attacks and data poisoning [[r2]]. The common thread is that **similarity is not authorization**: a nearest-neighbour search returns what is close to the query, and it has no idea who is asking.

explain.text: Inversion: vectors are not anonymised text

explain.md: A text embedding looks like opaque numbers, but Vec2Text recovered 92% of 32-token inputs exactly from embeddings produced by two embedding models, and it recovered full names from a dataset of clinical notes [[tr7]]. Treat vectors with the same classification, access rules and deletion rules as the source text.

explain.text: Cross-tenant exposure: a missing filter is a breach

explain.md: In a shared store the only wall is a filter on every query. The Azure Architecture Center says to apply a tenant discriminator and a user-level filter on every retrieval request, including those made inside an agent loop, and to put an API layer in front so other code cannot query the stores directly [[r22]].

explain.title: Design reasoning
explain.md: Result counts, scores and timing can also reveal that a hidden document exists. No source above measures this for RAG, so test whether your API exposes raw scores or counts to callers who should not learn that.

whereToUse: Shared vector stores used by several applications or tenants
Pipelines that export embeddings to analytics, evaluation or partner systems
Retention and deletion reviews of an index that holds personal or confidential text
Agent tools that accept a tenant id or filter as an argument

use: Several tenants or apps share a store
A deletion or offboarding obligation exists
avoid: Believing vectors are anonymous because they look like numbers
Letting the model or the client supply the tenant filter
Exporting raw vectors to broad-access analytics stores
flips: One tenant per store with physical isolation: cross-tenant risk drops but inversion and deletion remain
Embeddings never leave the service and the corpus is public: weigh integrity more than confidentiality

pitfalls.symptom: A tenant sees another tenant's snippet
pitfalls.cause: A tool or batch job queried the index without the tenant filter
pitfalls.fix: Route every query through one API layer that injects the filter from the authenticated identity

pitfalls.symptom: Embeddings sit in a shared analytics bucket
pitfalls.fix: Give them the source classification, or drop them from exports

pitfalls.cause: Old index versions, replicas or caches keep the vectors
pitfalls.fix: Delete by source id across every copy and test with a canary document

scenarios.title: Embeddings exported to analytics
scenarios.situation: A platform team wants to copy all document embeddings into a shared analytics warehouse for clustering. The text stays in the secured store. The team calls the vectors harmless numbers.
unknowns: Which classification do the source documents carry?
scenarios.question: How do you respond?

options.name: Export vectors but remove document ids
options.why: Removing ids does not stop inversion of the vector itself.
options.tradeoff: Acceptable for vectors made from public text.

options.name: Export only low-dimensional projections for clustering
options.why: Lowers exposure for analytics that do not need full vectors.
options.tradeoff: Quality drops and you must verify the projection is not invertible for your data.

options.name: Treat vectors as the same classification as the text and keep them inside the same access boundary
options.why: Inversion research shows embeddings can reconstruct text, so exposure of vectors is exposure of content.
options.tradeoff: Analytics must run inside the secured store or on a reduced set.

flips.then: Export is fine and only integrity matters.

flips.if: The warehouse has the same access controls as the source
flips.then: Export is acceptable, with deletion propagated.

scenarios.takeaway: Classify embeddings like their source text.

scenarios.title: Tenant id in a tool argument
scenarios.situation: A multi-tenant SaaS assistant uses a shared index. The retrieval tool takes a tenant id as an argument that the model fills in from conversation context.
unknowns: Is there an API layer in front of the index?
Can users influence the context the model sees?
scenarios.question: How do you fix the design?

options.name: Add a system prompt rule to always use the current tenant
options.why: A prompt rule is not enforcement, and injection can override it.
options.tradeoff: Fine as guidance on top of enforced filters.

options.name: Remove the argument: a gateway derives tenant and user filters from the authenticated request and injects them
options.why: The model can be steered by documents and users, so it must never choose the filter.
options.tradeoff: Tools lose flexibility for cross-tenant admin queries, which need a separate path.

options.name: Validate the tenant id the model supplies against the session
options.tradeoff: Still trusts the model to supply the other filter fields and needs careful coverage.

flips.if: A few tenants need hard isolation
flips.then: Give them a dedicated index or service and route by tenant.

flips.if: Agents call several tools in a loop
flips.then: Apply the same injected filter in every tool call.

scenarios.takeaway: The model never supplies an authorization filter.

scenarios.title: Offboarding a customer
scenarios.situation: A customer leaves and the contract requires removal of all their data within thirty days. Their chunks sit in a shared index, in a nightly export and in a cache.
unknowns: Is there a source id on every chunk?
How long do caches and exports live?
scenarios.question: What do you do?

options.name: Delete by tenant id across index, exports, caches and old index versions, then verify with a canary query
options.why: Vectors and cached answers are copies of the customer's data.
options.tradeoff: Needs tenant ids on every copy and a tested delete path.

options.name: Delete from the live index only
options.why: Exports and caches keep serving or storing the data.
options.tradeoff: Enough only when no other copy exists.

options.name: Rebuild the whole index without the tenant
options.tradeoff: Expensive for a shared index and still misses exports and caches.

flips.if: Each tenant has a dedicated index
flips.then: Deleting the index gives fast, complete offboarding for that store.
Keep the delete log, not the content.

scenarios.takeaway: Deletion must reach every copy of the vector and the text.

quiz.q: Why should embeddings of confidential documents carry the same classification as the documents?
options: Vector databases are slow to delete from
Inversion work has recovered exact text and personal names from embeddings
Embeddings are always larger than the text
Cosine similarity reveals the user's identity
quiz.explain: Vec2Text recovered 92% of 32-token inputs exactly and recovered full names from clinical notes. Size, deletion speed and identity leakage are unrelated to the classification argument.

quiz.q: Which are OWASP LLM08 mitigations for a shared vector store? Choose all that apply.
options: Permission-aware stores with strict logical partitioning
quiz.explain: OWASP lists permission-aware stores with logical and access partitioning, data validation with source authentication, tagging and classification, and immutable retrieval logs. A larger dimension does not address leakage.

flashcards.front: What does "similarity is not authorization" mean?
flashcards.back: Nearest-neighbour search returns what is close to the query and knows nothing about the caller. Permission checks must be added to the query or applied by another system.
Text embeddings can be inverted: 92% of 32-token inputs recovered exactly from embeddings of two models, and full names from clinical notes. Treat vectors as sensitive as the text.

flashcards.front: What does the Architecture Center advise for shared RAG stores?
flashcards.back: A tenant discriminator and user-level filter on every retrieval, an API layer in front of the stores, filters inside agent loops too, and access logs of grounding data.
